item.title: [6] The piezochiral effect
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Authors: Z. Zeng, M. Först, M. Fechner, X. Deng, A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Novel strain-controlled chirality effect, relevant to symmetry breaking and spintronics.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #theory #spintronics #chirality

Abstract: The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

item.title: [6] Perpendicular switching of polarization in layered ferroelectrics
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Javier Junquera, Ramamoorthy Ramesh

Authors: Pushpendra Gupta, Sergio Puebla, Fernando Gómez-Ortiz, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Control of polarization in layered oxides, adjacent to the user's material interests.

Tags: #material #ferroelectrics #layered-materials

Abstract: Perpendicular switching of the polarization state in the layered ferroelectric Bi4Ti3O12 is demonstrated by means of trilinear coupling, allowing manipulation of the in-plane polarization component with an out-of-plane electric field.

item.title: [7] A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Daniel Zehnder, Andrew Ziegler

Authors: Michael Abraham, Edwin Acuna, Tower S. Adams, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental quantum computing hardware using silicon and superconducting components; important quantum materials development.

Tags: #quantumcomputing #superconductivity #silicon

Abstract: A silicon quantum processing unit executes high-fidelity multiqubit circuits, with all time-varying control signals generated by a digitally programmed cryogenic complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor controller and delivered to the low-noise, exchange-only qubit device through a high-density superconducting ribbon cable.

item.title: [6] Plasmonic metamaterial time crystal
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Marco Schirò, Yannis Laplace

Authors: Tingwen Guo, Jules Sueiro, Gian Marcello Andolina, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Experimental plasmonic metamaterial demonstrating time crystal phenomena; adjacent condensed matter interest.

Tags: #metamaterials #plasmonics #timecrystal

Abstract: A plasmonic metamaterial driven at terahertz frequencies achieves strong, ultrafast temporal modulation and shows a transition to the photonic time crystal regime with reduced plasmonic losses.

item.title: [6] Photocatalytic water splitting by 2D polymer with out-of-plane carrier flow
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Kazunari Domen, Xinchen Wang

Authors: Hangyu Zhuzhang, Zhiyang Yu, Xiaocong Liang, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: 2D polymer with electronic properties for photocatalysis, hints at STS, relevant to materials physics.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #polymers #photocatalysis #electronicproperties

Abstract: A strategy using polymeric carbon nitride crystals induces out-of-plane carrier migration by means of internal electric fields applied on facet-selective nanofilms placed on polymer photocatalysts, increasing the apparent quantum efficiency for overall water splitting.

item.content:encoded:

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of unconventional ferroelectric thin film properties, relevant functional materials physics.

Abstract: Coupling between horizontal and vertical electric polarization enables an unconventional ferroelectric material to be controlled using standard device geometry.
